## What This Repository Is

`memq-bench` is the public, reproducible benchmark harness for measuring hosted
MemQ against Mem0 OSS, keyword retrieval, and no-memory controls. MemQ is
evaluated as the hosted, governed MCP fabric exposed at `mcp.multinex.ai`, not
as an embedded local vector helper.

## Source-of-Truth Artifacts

Use checked-in artifacts instead of summarizing from memory:

- Retrieval snapshot: `artifacts/snapshot.json`
- Retrieval summary: `artifacts/summary.md`

- LLM answer snapshot: `artifacts/llm-snapshot.json`

| `memq_mcp` | 36 | 36 | 0 | 100% | 100% | 100% | 100% | 13 ms | 25 ms |
| `mem0_oss` | 36 | 36 | 0 | 58% | 100% | 100% | 67% | 2511 ms | 2814 ms |
| `keyword_baseline` | 36 | 36 | 0 | 58% | 100% | 92% | 67% | 0 ms | 0 ms |

Artifact-backed retrieval comparison:

- Hosted MemQ MCP beats Mem0 OSS by +42 points on primary@1.
- Hosted MemQ MCP matches Mem0 OSS on recall@K.
- Hosted MemQ MCP is 100% leakage-free in the checked-in retrieval run.
- Hosted MemQ MCP averages 13 ms retrieval versus 2511 ms for Mem0 OSS in this setup.

Do not conflate this older same-model LLM answer snapshot with the newer
retrieval snapshot. A fresh LLM rerun should be published only after provider
quota is available and the artifacts are regenerated.

## Benchmark Layers

1. Retrieval benchmark
   - Providers: `memq_mcp`, `mem0_oss`, `keyword_baseline`
   - Measures ranking quality, leakage resistance, recall, precision, MRR, and latency.
   - Primary command: `npm run bench`
2. Same-model answer benchmark
   - Conditions: `no_memory`, `keyword_context`, `memq_context`, `mem0_context`
   - Measures whether retrieved context improves final answers for the same model.
   - Primary command: `npm run bench:llm`

## Reproduction Commands

```bash
npm install
npm run setup:mem0
docker compose up -d qdrant falkordb
export MEMQ_API_KEY_AUTH_HEADER="Bearer <your MemQ API token>"
npm run type-check
npm run bench
npm run bench:llm
```

`npm run bench` writes `artifacts/snapshot.json`.
`npm run bench:llm` writes `artifacts/llm-snapshot.json`.

## Hosted MemQ MCP Client Shape

Use an environment variable for credentials. Do not paste real tokens into
checked-in files or public prompts.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "memq": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "mcp-remote",
        "https://mcp.multinex.ai/mcp/v1",
        "--header",
        "Authorization:${MEMQ_API_KEY_AUTH_HEADER}"
      ],
      "env": {
        "MEMQ_API_KEY_AUTH_HEADER": "Bearer <your MemQ API token>"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Public Claim Guardrails

Allowed, when citing the current checked-in retrieval artifact:

- Hosted MemQ MCP reaches 100% primary@1 on the checked-in retrieval benchmark.
- Hosted MemQ MCP reaches 100% leakage-free retrieval on the checked-in retrieval benchmark.
- Hosted MemQ MCP averages 13 ms retrieval in the checked-in retrieval run.
- MemQ leads Mem0 OSS by +42 points on primary@1 in the checked-in retrieval run.

Avoid:

- Claiming the LLM answer snapshot is as fresh as the retrieval snapshot.
- Claiming benchmark results prove every possible workload.
- Claiming MemQ private namespace data is written to `_commons`.
- Publishing secrets, raw API keys, private tenant data, or unsanitized source content.

## Repository Map

- `src/retrievalCli.ts`: retrieval benchmark CLI
- `src/retrievalHarness.ts`: retrieval benchmark execution
- `src/retrievalProviders.ts`: provider wiring for hosted MemQ, Mem0 OSS, and keyword baseline
- `src/llmCli.ts`: same-model LLM answer benchmark CLI
- `src/llmHarness.ts`: LLM answer benchmark execution
- `src/retrievalSchemas.ts`: typed retrieval artifacts
- `src/llmSchemas.ts`: typed LLM answer artifacts
- `configs/retrieval-smoke.json`: primary retrieval run manifest
- `configs/llm-answer-smoke.json`: primary LLM answer run manifest
- `skills/`: reusable MemQ agent skills and hook templates

## Namespace And Commons Notes

Team and private memory ingestion stay namespace-scoped. The global `_commons`
surface is explicit and governed; benchmark material should not imply that
random team or private memories can poison or pollute `_commons`.
